speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; please tell me when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse over time. Additionally, have you noticed any weakness, numbness, or issues with your balance or vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" gait suggests a cerebellar issue. You mentioned clumsiness on the right side specifically; does this ataxia affect both legs equally, or is one leg more affected than the other? Also, have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or double vision recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history is highly concerning given your use of natalizumab for Crohn's disease; have you noticed any new changes in your speech, coordination, or eye movements specifically? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES.

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

The MRI results confirm multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, which is characteristic of PML, especially given your history of Crohn's disease and use of natalizumab. This is a serious opportunistic infection of the white matter caused by the JC virus.

I have reached my limit for questions. Please ensure your treating team is immediately aware of the PML risk associated with your current medication.
